title: False Cognates - Contextual Concept Collapsing
pattern: Attempting to unify completely different concepts under a single generic type because they share the same homonym in English.
why_bad: It creates a bloated, confusing structure riddled with nullable fields and conditional branches. It violates boundary principles, making it impossible to enforce invariants since the struct represents different concepts in different contexts.
detection: Identify structs containing large clusters of optional fields that are never populated together, accompanied by variable naming that shifts meaning based on the call path.
counterexample: None. Reusing homonyms for completely separate business meanings is a fundamental modeling defect. `Strong`.
fix: Establish distinct models within distinct namespaces (e.g., `BankingAccount` and `LiteraryAccount`).
source: *Domain-Driven Design* by Eric Evans (2003), p. 335, 456; *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (2013), p. 72.
